reading.body:
CyrusOne Norwalk holds 4 MW of IT capacity, ranking first among Connecticut's two facilities with disclosed power and representing half the state's announced 8 MW total.

This facility occupies 168,000 square feet of technical space in Norwalk, Connecticut and carries SSAE 16 Type II certification for security and availability controls. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the published capacity translates to roughly 100 racks, sufficient for a single mid-scale training cluster. Connecticut's mapped footprint includes only five facilities, suggesting early-stage infrastructure development for AI workloads in the state.

The Northeast's grid constraints and land costs create structural limits on AI expansion in Connecticut relative to regions with cheaper power and space. Norwalk's 4 MW is modest for frontier AI training or inference at published scale. Its value lies as part of regional supply only if the operator expands capacity or if three unmapped Connecticut facilities hold significant undisclosed power. The data covers published capacity only, so actual deployable compute may exceed these figures.
